newsitem.title: USA: Wash. Water Power sets residential pilot.
newsitem.headline: Wash. Water Power sets residential pilot.

text.p: Washington Water Power Co on Thursday announced plans for a pilot program allowing a small portion of residential and commercial customers to choose an alternate energy supplier to serve their electric load.
WWP said it plans to file the plan with the Washington Utilities and Transportation Commission and the Idaho Public Utilities Commission.

Tom Dukich, Washington Water Power manager of rates and tariffs, said the company proposed the pilot in response to growing interest in assessing the potential benefits of direct access to small customers, and to collect information that would assist in the transition to customer choice.
If approved, the pilot program would run for two years beginning July 1, 1997.
It would apply to about 2,500 residential and 300 commercial customers, who would be under no obligation to sign up with alternate suppliers.
Participating alternate suppliers would pay a fee for each customer that they sign up. These fees would cover a portion of Washington Water Power's administrative costs and lost margins.
